title: Probate a will or qualify as executor or administrator
question: Someone died owning property in Staunton. How do we probate the will or get appointed to handle the estate?
audience: families of people who have died
office: Clerk of the Circuit Court for the City of Staunton (elected constitutional officer), Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office, 25th Judicial Circuit
summary: If the person who died lived in the City of Staunton, the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office (Cochran Judicial Center, 3rd floor, 113 E. Beverley Street; 540.332.3874) probates the will and appoints the executor or administrator; the Clerk acts as probate judge. Call ahead, fill in the City's Probate Information Form, and bring the original will, a copy of the death certificate and asset values. You take an oath, give bond, file a List of Heirs, and pay the state probate tax (10 cents per $100 on estates over $15,000), the city's one-third share and a qualification fee. Within 30 days of qualifying or probate, send notice to the spouse, heirs and beneficiaries; within four months, file an inventory with the Commissioner of Accounts (unless the Clerk waives it for a small estate). Clerk's orders can be appealed to the circuit court within six months.

legal_basis.citation: Staunton City Code § 3.70.010 (Chapter 3.70, Probate Tax: Local probate tax; on eCode360, paraphrased in steps, fees and caveats, not quoted)

steps.step: Confirm that the Staunton Circuit Court is the right court
steps.who: The person holding the will, the named executor, or a family member
steps.how: Wills are probated, and administrators appointed, in the circuit court of the county or city where the person who died lived. If they lived in the City of Staunton, go to the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office. A Staunton mailing address does not settle it: a person who lived in Augusta County goes to the separate Augusta Circuit Court (Augusta County Courthouse, 100 Dick Huff Lane, Verona), and a Waynesboro resident to the Waynesboro Circuit Court (250 South Wayne Avenue, Waynesboro). The Staunton, Augusta and Waynesboro circuit courts are separate courts with separate clerks, although all three belong to the 25th Judicial Circuit. The City's Probate Information Form asks whether the decedent was a City of Staunton resident. A person who became a patient in a nursing home, convalescent home or similar institution because of age or ill health is presumed to keep the residence they had before (the presumption can be rebutted); the form asks where the person lived before entering a nursing home. If the person had no known place of residence in a Virginia county or city, the will goes where real estate they owned or left by will lies, and if there is none, where they died or have property. A will already proved in another state can be offered here as an authenticated copy with its certificate of probate.
steps.deadline: No set time; the Virginia Court Clerks' Association pamphlet linked from the City's probate page recommends starting the initial steps within 30 days after death
steps.quote: A will shall be offered for probate in the circuit court in the county or city wherein the decedent has a known place of residence

steps.step: Until qualifying, the named executor only handles the funeral and protects the property
steps.who: The person named as executor in the will
steps.how: A named executor has no power to act for the estate until qualifying before the Clerk. Before that, they may only arrange the burial, pay reasonable funeral expenses and keep property from being wasted. Keep the original will (and any codicils) safe, because the originals must be brought to the Clerk. The Clerk can require anyone holding the will to produce it.
steps.quote: A person named in a will as executor shall not exercise the powers of executor until he qualifies as such by taking an oath and giving bond in the court or before the clerk where the will or an authenticated copy thereof is admitted to record, except that he may provide for the burial of the testator, pay reasonable funeral expenses, and preserve the estate from waste.

steps.step: Decide whether someone needs to qualify, or whether the will only needs to be probated
steps.how: Probate covers only the decedent's probate estate. Property owned with someone else with a right of survivorship, life insurance not payable to the estate, real estate passing by a transfer on death deed and other property passing by contract or beneficiary designation pass outside it; the City's form asks only for personal assets held in the decedent's name (accounts without a joint holder or a beneficiary). If the whole personal probate estate is $75,000 or less, at least 60 days have passed since the death, and no application to appoint a personal representative is pending or has been granted anywhere, all known successors can sign a Small Estate Affidavit (CC-1685), each signature notarized (the form's jurat also offers a clerk or deputy clerk), and give it to whoever holds the asset, without anyone qualifying. The City's probate page links a City-hosted copy of the affidavit; the statewide form is listed here. The affidavit states that any will was duly probated, so a will still goes to the Clerk; the clerk's-office section of the City's form lists 'Probate of Will only' as an appointment type. The City's page also links the DMV's guide to the vehicle and license records of a person who has died.
steps.deadline: At least 60 days after the death (small estate affidavit)
steps.quote: this form should only be used when the value of the deceased person's entire personal probate estate as of the date of death does not exceed $75,000.

steps.step: Call the Clerk's Office to arrange the probate or qualification
steps.who: The person offering the will, or the person asking to be appointed
steps.how: Telephone the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office at 540.332.3874 before going. The City's probate page does not say probate is by appointment only, but the City's form speaks of 'the appointment', the statewide CC-1650 instructions say to call for one, and the Virginia Court Clerks' Association pamphlet linked from the City's page recommends making an appointment with the Clerk or a deputy clerk. Office hours are 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, and the Clerk's page says all transactions requiring payment must be done before 4:30 p.m. The office mailbox the City lists on its Public Records Request page for estate information is circuitcourtclerk@ci.staunton.va.us.
steps.quote: You should telephone the Clerk's Office for an appointment before you go to the courthouse.

steps.step: Fill in the City of Staunton Probate Information Form and gather what to bring
steps.who: The person offering the will, or each person asking to be appointed
steps.how: Download the City of Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office Probate Information Form from the probate page and fill it in. It asks for the decedent's name as on the death certificate and as on the will, marital status, last address, dates of birth and death, place of death, whether they were a Staunton resident or in a nursing home, and the dates of the will and any codicils. Each proposed executor or administrator answers questions on legal disability, felony convictions, bankruptcy and law licensing, and gives contact details and any attorney. List every heir at law (next of kin under Va. Code § 64.2-200), even those who inherit nothing under the will, with age, address and relationship. Give the value of personal assets in the decedent's name only, and the address, locality and fair market value of real estate in and outside Virginia. Bring the original will and every codicil (the statewide instructions say to bring all originals) and a copy of the death certificate, which the clerks' pamphlet linked from the City's page says to take; the form's clerk's-office section records the proof of death (a death certificate or other).

steps.step: Prove the will before the Clerk
steps.who: The person offering the will, with the will's witnesses if needed; the Clerk or a deputy clerk
steps.how: In Staunton the Clerk acts as probate judge: the Clerk authenticates the will, holds a hearing with witnesses, appoints the executor or administrator and prepares the orders. If the will has a self-proving affidavit (the testator and witnesses swore to it before a notary), no witness needs to come. If not, bring at least one of the will's witnesses. A will wholly in the testator's handwriting must be proved by at least two disinterested witnesses: bring two people who know the handwriting and are not relatives, beneficiaries or relatives of beneficiaries; they swear to it before the Clerk or a deputy clerk on CC-1604 (the same form serves for the will of a person in military service). A witness who lives outside Virginia, or lives in Virginia but cannot testify before the Clerk for any reason (the statewide instructions mention sickness, age and legal confinement), can give a deposition instead, sworn before a clerk, deputy clerk or notary public: CC-1601 for a witness to a will without a self-proving clause, CC-1602 for a witness to a handwritten will, and CC-1603 to prove the signatures of attesting witnesses who have died and of the testator. For a deposition, the person offering the will may withdraw it for a time, leaving an attested copy with the Clerk, or get a certified copy. The Clerk may require all of the testator's will papers to be produced.
steps.quote: The Clerk ensures the authentication of the will, conducts a legal hearing with witnesses, makes a legal appointment of an executor or administrator of a decedent’s estate and prepares legal documents and orders related to the handling of the estate.

steps.step: If there is no will, or the named executor will not serve, work out who may be appointed
steps.who: Heirs (distributees), residuary or substantial beneficiaries, creditors
steps.how: With no will: during the first 30 days after death the Clerk may appoint a sole heir (distributee) or that heir's designee or, if there is no sole heir, an heir or designee who brings written waivers of the right to qualify (CC-1608) from all the other competent heirs. After 30 days, the first heir or designee who applies may be appointed, but if more than one heir told the Clerk within those 30 days that they mean to qualify, all of them must first be given a chance to be heard. After 45 days, a nonprofit charitable organization that was the decedent's conservator or guardian may be appointed after a diligent search and certified-mail notice to any sole heir. After 60 days, a creditor or another person may be appointed after certifying a diligent search and a certified-mail notice to any sole heir at least 30 days before applying, or that no address could be found (CC-1609). If the will names no executor, or the named executor refuses, fails to give bond, dies, resigns or is removed, administration with the will annexed may go to a residual or substantial legatee under the will or their designee; if no such person applies within 30 days, to a person who would have been entitled to administration if there had been no will. Administration is not granted to anyone under a legal disability (Va. Code § 8.01-2), and the Clerk must be satisfied the person is suitable and competent. An administrator of an estate without a will also signs under oath that they are not under a disability and have not been convicted of a felony of fraud or misrepresentation, robbery, extortion, burglary, larceny, embezzlement, fraudulent conversion, perjury, bribery, treason or racketeering; a sole heir with such a conviction may still be appointed if otherwise suitable and competent. A spouse or parent barred from the estate for desertion or abandonment may not serve as administrator if a beneficiary objects. The City's form asks every proposed executor or administrator about disability, felony convictions, bankruptcy and law licensing.
steps.deadline: First 30 days after death: sole heir, or an heir with waivers; after 30 days: first heir who applies; after 60 days: creditor or other person
steps.quote: After 30 days have passed since the decedent's death, the court or the clerk may grant administration to the first distributee, or his designee, who applies

steps.step: If an executor or administrator lives outside Virginia, arrange a Virginia resident
steps.who: A nonresident executor or administrator, and a Virginia resident co-fiduciary or agent
steps.how: The City's form says that if the person seeking appointment is not a Virginia resident, a Virginia resident must either co-qualify as executor or administrator or be appointed as 'the resident' (the form's wording is garbled; read with the statewide CC-1610, it points to a Virginia resident appointed to receive service of process). A co-qualifying Virginia resident must come to the appointment too. State law itself lets a nonresident qualify alone: at qualification the nonresident files a written consent (CC-1610) that legal papers may be served on the Clerk or on a Virginia resident they name, and must give bond with surety even if the will waives surety, unless a Virginia resident personal representative qualifies at the same time or the Clerk, in its discretion, allows a bond without surety because no more than $35,000 will come into the fiduciary's hands. The clerks' pamphlet linked from the City's page adds that a nonresident co-fiduciary cannot qualify without surety if the Virginia resident serving with them cannot. Ask the Clerk whether Staunton insists on a resident co-fiduciary or agent in every case.

steps.step: Go to the Clerk's Office on the third floor of the Cochran Judicial Center
steps.who: Everyone who must appear: the person offering the will, each person qualifying, and any witness
steps.how: The Clerk's Office is on the 3rd floor of the George M. Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street. The City's visitor page lists the New Street and Johnson Street parking garages, metered lots and limited street parking; accessible parking is on New Street, with an accessible rear door with a call button, and an elevator. Under the Staunton Circuit Court's Policy Regarding Portable Electronic Devices (posted on vacourts.gov, entered 6/10/2026), phones, computers and other portable electronic devices are not allowed in the courthouse except for listed groups such as attorneys and officials on duty, or a visitor whom the Sheriff determines poses no security risk and needs the device for their business at the courthouse; free storage is provided at the security entrance. Bring paper copies of anything you need. The visitor page also says food, drink and weapons are not permitted in the building.
steps.quote: Located on the 3rd floor of the Cochran Judicial Center at 113 E. Beverley Street, Staunton, VA 24401

steps.step: File the probate tax return and pay the state and city probate tax
steps.who: The person offering the will or asking for administration; the Clerk collects the tax
steps.how: If the estate is worth more than $15,000, file the confidential Probate Tax Return (CC-1651) with the Clerk when the will is offered or administration is sought. Give the value of Virginia real estate (the assessed value for local real estate tax is accepted if you do not know the actual value; real estate outside Virginia is left out) and an estimate of the personal property at the date of death (the form's instructions say the Clerk accepts a reasonable estimate). Only the probate estate counts: survivorship property, life insurance not payable to the estate, transfer on death real estate and other property passing by contract or beneficiary designation are left out. Pay the state tax at the Clerk's Office; no one can qualify as executor or administrator until it is paid. Staunton also has a city probate tax of one-third of the state tax, which the Clerk collects and pays into the city treasury. City Code § 3.70.010, as read on eCode360, imposes it on grants of administration and does not mention the probate of wills, so ask the Clerk whether the city share is also charged when a will is probated with an executor. If the later inventory shows a higher value, the Clerk collects the extra tax; nothing is charged or refunded when the difference is under $25.
steps.deadline: At the time the will is offered for probate or administration is sought
steps.fee: State: 10 cents per $100 of value or fraction of $100 (no tax on estates of $15,000 or less); City of Staunton: one-third of the state tax (charged on grants of administration; confirm with the Clerk for probate with an executor)
steps.quote: No one shall be permitted to qualify and act as executor or administrator until the tax imposed by § 58.1-1712 has been paid.

steps.step: Take the oath and sign the bond
steps.who: Each executor or administrator, before the Clerk or a deputy clerk
steps.how: Each executor or administrator swears to perform the duties faithfully (an executor or administrator with the will annexed also swears the writing is the true last will, so far as they know; an administrator of an estate without a will swears that, so far as they know, there is no will) and signs a bond for at least the full value of the personal estate, plus the real estate or its rents and profits if the will authorizes selling the real estate or receiving the rents. Surety is required unless the will waives it, or all heirs or all beneficiaries under the will are personal representatives (or one is the only heir or beneficiary because the others disclaimed); the Clerk may also, in its discretion, allow a bond without surety when there are no assets or no more than $35,000 will come into the fiduciary's hands. A nonresident must give surety even if the will waives it (step s8). Surety is normally a surety bond bought from an insurance company and paid for from estate assets; the clerk's-office section of the City's form records whether the will waives surety and the surety company. An heir, beneficiary or other person with a financial interest can later ask the court to require security. Pay the qualification fee.
steps.fee: Qualification fee: $20 for estates up to $50,000, $25 up to $100,000, $30 over $100,000; none for estates of $5,000 or less (statutory). The statute also sets $3 for making out a bond and administering the oaths; whether Staunton charges it separately was not confirmed. Any surety bond premium is extra.
steps.quote: The court or clerk shall require a personal representative to furnish security.

steps.who: The executor or administrator (or the person offering the will if no one qualifies)
steps.how: Sign the List of Heirs (CC-1611) under oath, giving every heir at law with address, relationship and age (if known), whether or not there is a will; the heirs listed on the City's form are the starting point. File it with the Clerk when you qualify (or, if no one qualifies, when the will is presented), and with the clerk of any other city or county where the decedent's real estate lies. You cannot be paid for your work until it is filed, unless you file an affidavit with the Commissioner of Accounts that the heirs are unknown to you after diligent inquiry. The list shows the heirs on the date of death; if that changes, file an additional list. If no one has qualified within 30 days of the death of a person without a will, an heir may file a list of heirs alone.
steps.deadline: At the time of qualification (or when the will is presented, if no one qualifies)
steps.fee: Recording cost is paid from the estate. When no will is probated and no administration is granted, recording a list of heirs costs the $25 state fee.
steps.quote: furnish a list of heirs under oath in accordance with a form provided to each clerk of court by the Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court

steps.step: Get the order and the certificate of qualification
steps.who: The Clerk of the Staunton Circuit Court or a deputy clerk
steps.how: The Clerk enters the order admitting the will and appointing you, records the will in the will book, and may issue a certificate of qualification, which has the same effect as formal probate or letters of administration; if you ask, the Clerk must make out the probate or letters in due form, signed by the Clerk, sealed and certified by the judge. If the Clerk let you qualify without surety under the $35,000 rule, the Clerk issues certificates titled 'Qualification Certificate for Small Asset Estate', each limited to that amount. At qualification the Clerk also gives you a written statement that you are responsible for filing tax returns and accounting for the estate, and the notice forms for the next step. Ask how many certified copies you need.
steps.fee: Copies: $0.50 per page; $2 for attaching the court seal and the clerk's certificate (statutory amounts)
steps.quote: The court or clerk may issue a certificate of qualification to any personal representative for obtaining probate or letters of administration, which shall be given the same effect as the probate or letters made out in due form.

steps.step: Send notice to the spouse, heirs and beneficiaries
steps.who: The executor or administrator, or the person who probated the will
steps.how: Use the Notice Regarding Estate (CC-1616). Deliver it, or mail it first-class postage prepaid, at their last known addresses to the surviving spouse, all heirs at law (even when there is a will), the living and ascertained beneficiaries under the will (including beneficiaries of any trust it creates), and beneficiaries under any earlier will of the decedent probated in the same court. The notice gives the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's mailing address and that of the Commissioner of Accounts. No notice is needed for a personal representative or proponent, anyone who signed a Waiver of Notice (CC-1618), a person summoned to a show-cause hearing on the will, a person under conservatorship or guardianship whose conservator or guardian is notified, a non-heir whose gift of money or personal belongings is $10,000 or less, and the others listed in Va. Code § 64.2-508(B). Anyone with an interest in the estate may give the notice. The notice tells them they may ask in writing for copies of the inventory and accounts.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the date of qualification or admission of the will to probate
steps.quote: Within 30 days after the date of qualification or admission of the will to probate, a personal representative or proponent of the will shall forward notice by delivery or by first-class mail, postage prepaid, to the persons entitled to notice at their last known address.

steps.who: The executor or administrator, or the person who probated the will
steps.how: Sign the Affidavit of Notice Regarding Estate (CC-1617), listing who was sent the notice and when, or stating that no notice was required, and record it at the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office. Anyone with an interest in the estate may record it. The Commissioner of Accounts cannot approve the estate's settlement until it is recorded, and summons a fiduciary who has not done it four months after qualification.
steps.deadline: Within four months (after qualification or probate)
steps.quote: The personal representative or proponent of the will shall record within four months in the clerk's office where the will is recorded an affidavit stating

steps.step: Record the will and list of heirs wherever the decedent's Virginia real estate lies
steps.how: If the decedent owned, or left by will, real estate in another Virginia city or county, record a certified copy of the will at that circuit court clerk's office and file the list of heirs there too; the City's form asks about real estate outside Staunton and outside Virginia. The same applies in reverse: when someone who lived elsewhere in Virginia owned land in Staunton, the will probated at home is recorded, and the list of heirs filed, at the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office, which keeps the city's land records. When there was no will, anyone with an interest in the decedent's real estate may record a Real Estate Affidavit (CC-1612) where the land lies, so the land records show the heirs; that clerk sends an abstract to the local commissioner of the revenue, who may transfer the land on the land books.
steps.fee: Recording fee by page count (statutory); $25 state fee for a list of heirs or real estate affidavit when no will is probated and no administration is granted
steps.quote: The personal representative of the testator shall cause a certified copy of any will or of any authenticated copy so admitted to record to be recorded in any county or city wherein there is any real estate of which the testator possessed at the time of his death or that is devised by his will.

steps.step: File the inventory with the Commissioner of Accounts
steps.who: The executor or administrator; reviewed by a Commissioner of Accounts appointed by the Staunton Circuit Court
steps.how: List the estate's assets at their market value on the date of death on the Inventory for Decedent's Estate (CC-1670): the personal estate under your control, the decedent's interest in any multiple party account, real estate you have power to sell, and other real estate that is an estate asset, in Virginia or not. File it with the Commissioner of Accounts (the statewide directory lists the commissioners for Staunton; or ask the Clerk). Mail a copy to each entitled person who asked in writing for one. Report assets found later within four months of finding them. The commissioner charges a filing fee set by the court. The Clerk compares the inventory with the probate tax return and collects any additional tax. Exception: when the personal estate passing by will or without a will is $35,000 or less and an heir, a beneficiary or a creditor whose claim exceeds the estate qualifies, the Clerk shall waive the inventory and the settlement of accounts, unless the decedent owned real estate the fiduciary would have power to sell.
steps.deadline: Within four months after the date of the order conferring authority (qualification)
steps.fee: Commissioner of Accounts filing fee, set by the Staunton Circuit Court
steps.quote: Every personal representative or curator shall, within four months after the date of the order conferring his authority, return to the commissioner of accounts an inventory of all the personal estate under his supervision and control

steps.step: File accounts until the estate is settled
steps.how: File the first account (CC-1680) with the Commissioner of Accounts, covering the first 12 months; later accounts cover each following 12-month period until the estate is settled. The commissioner may extend a later deadline for reasonable cause, and you may file earlier. When all heirs (distributees) or all residuary beneficiaries are personal representatives, a Statement in Lieu of Settlement of Account (CC-1681) may be filed instead, once all known charges are paid, six months have passed since qualification and the residue is delivered; if it cannot be filed in time, file an interim account or a sworn notice of intent within the account deadline. The clerks' pamphlet linked from the City's page says to report any change of address or telephone number to the Commissioner of Accounts at once. File the income, inheritance or estate tax returns the law requires.
steps.deadline: Within 16 months from the date of qualification; later accounts within four months after the end of each 12-month period (the commissioner may extend for reasonable cause)
steps.fee: Commissioner of Accounts filing fee, set by the Staunton Circuit Court
steps.quote: Within 16 months from the date of the qualification, personal representatives shall exhibit before the commissioner of accounts a statement of all money and other property that the fiduciary has received, has become chargeable with, or has disbursed within 12 months from the date of qualification.

fees.item: State probate tax (wills probated and grants of administration)
fees.amount: 10 cents per $100 of estate value or fraction of $100; none for estates of $15,000 or less
fees.quote: For every $100 of value, or fraction of $100, a tax of 10 cent(s) is imposed.

fees.amount: One-third of the state probate tax (in effect 3.33 cents per $100 on estates over $15,000), collected by the Clerk and paid into the city treasury. City Code § 3.70.010 imposes it on grants of administration; whether it is also charged when a will is probated with an executor was not confirmed.
fees.basis: Staunton City Code § 3.70.010 (https://ecode360.com/49100424; read on eCode360, not quoted); the quote is from the enabling statute, Va. Code § 58.1-1718
fees.quote: impose a county or city tax in an amount equal to one-third of the amount of the state tax on the probate of a will or grant of administration

fees.item: Fee for appointing and qualifying an executor or administrator
fees.quote: $20 for estates not exceeding $50,000, $25 for estates not exceeding $100,000 and $30 for estates exceeding $100,000.

fees.item: No qualification fee for small estates
fees.quote: No fee shall be charged for estates of $5,000 or less.

fees.item: Recording and indexing a writing in the proper book (for example the will book)
fees.amount: $18 (10 or fewer pages); $32 (11 to 30 pages); $52 (31 or more pages)
fees.quote: $18 for an instrument or document consisting of 10 or fewer pages or sheets; $32 for an instrument or document consisting of 11 to 30 pages or sheets; and $52 for an instrument or document consisting of 31 or more pages or sheets

fees.item: Making out a bond and administering the oaths
fees.quote: For making out any bond, other than those under § 17.1-267 or subdivision A 4, administering all necessary oaths and writing proper affidavits, $3.

fees.item: State fee for recording a list of heirs or real estate affidavit when no will is probated and no administration is granted
fees.quote: A $25 fee is hereby charged on the recordation of a list of heirs pursuant to § 64.2-509 or an affidavit pursuant to § 64.2-510 unless a will has been probated for the decedent or there has been a grant of administration on the decedent's estate.

fees.item: Additional probate tax (or refund) after the inventory shows a different value
fees.amount: The difference; none charged or refunded if under $25
fees.quote: No additional tax shall be payable or no refund made if the payment or refund due would be less than twenty-five dollars.

fees.item: Copies of court papers (for example the will or the qualification order)
fees.quote: For making out a copy of any paper, record, or electronic record to go out of the office, which is not otherwise specifically provided for herein, a fee of $0.50 for each page or, if an electronic record, each image.

fees.item: Court seal and clerk's certificate on a copy (certified copy)
fees.amount: $2 (plus $0.50 if the judge's certificate is requested)
fees.quote: For annexing the seal of the court to any paper, writing the certificate of the clerk accompanying it, the clerk shall charge $2 and for attaching the certificate of the judge, if the clerk is requested to do so, the clerk shall charge an additional $0.50.

fees.item: Convenience fee if paying the Clerk by credit or debit card (where cards are accepted)
fees.amount: Up to 4 percent of the payment or a flat $2 per transaction
fees.quote: Such convenience fee shall not exceed four percent of the amount paid for the transaction or a flat fee of $2 per transaction.

fees.item: Surety bond premium (when surety is not waived)
fees.amount: Set by the surety company; paid from estate assets
fees.quote: This is normally done by purchasing a surety bond from an insurance company and paying for it out of estate assets.

fees.item: Commissioner of Accounts fees (inventory, accounts, statements in lieu)
fees.amount: Set by the Staunton Circuit Court; no Staunton schedule was found. The statewide guideline effective January 1, 2023 lists, for example, $135.00 to $350.00 for an inventory and $275.00 to $1,650.00 (plus .00075 over $1,000,000, and $5.00 for mailing) for a first account, by asset value, and $250.00 for a statement in lieu of settlement or a notice of intent to file one.
fees.basis: Uniform Fee Schedule Guidelines for Commissioners of Accounts (the quote's source), https://www.vacourts.gov/static/courts/circuit/resources/coa/coa_fee_schedule.pdf; see also https://www.vacourts.gov/courts/circuit/resources/coa/home
fees.quote: By statute, each Circuit Court sets the fees for its Commissioner(s) of Accounts

escalation.trigger: A person interested in the probate of the will disagrees with an order the Clerk entered under § 64.2-444, such as admitting or refusing the will or appointing an executor or administrator
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court (a judge), which hears the matter anew (de novo)
escalation.deadline: Within six months after the Clerk's order
escalation.quote: Any person interested in the probate of the will may appeal any order entered pursuant to § 64.2-444 within six months after the entering of such an order, without giving any bond, to the circuit court whose clerk, or deputy, has made the order.

escalation.trigger: More than one heir wants to be administrator
escalation.next: The Clerk or the court, which must give every heir who gave notice an opportunity to be heard before appointing anyone
escalation.deadline: Notify the Clerk during the first 30 days after the death
escalation.quote: more than one distributee notifies the court or the clerk of an intent to qualify after the 30-day period has elapsed, the court or the clerk shall not grant administration to any distributee, or his designee, until the court or the clerk has given all such distributees an opportunity to be heard.

escalation.trigger: The order of appointment in the statute would not serve the estate
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court, which may appoint another suitable person
escalation.quote: if the court determines that it is in the best interests of a decedent's estate, the court may depart from the provisions of this section at any time and grant administration to such person as the court deems appropriate.

escalation.trigger: The will's validity is doubtful or a dispute is expected before probate
escalation.next: Ask the Clerk to summon everyone interested to show cause why the will should not be probated; the Staunton Circuit Court then hears the motion (with a jury if anyone interested asks)
escalation.quote: may request that the clerk of such court summon any person interested in the probate of the will to appear to show cause why the will should not be admitted to probate.

escalation.trigger: Estate property is at risk while the will is contested or before anyone qualifies
escalation.next: Ask the Clerk or the Staunton Circuit Court to appoint a curator to protect the estate
escalation.quote: may appoint a curator of the estate of a decedent during a contest about the decedent's will, during the infancy or in the absence of an executor, or until administration of the estate be granted

escalation.trigger: An interested person who was not part of the Clerk's proceeding wants to contest the will, or to establish a will
escalation.next: Complaint to impeach or establish the will in circuit court (jury trial)
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the Clerk's or court's order (two years if served only by order of publication)
escalation.quote: may file a complaint to impeach or establish the will within one year from the date of the order entered by the court in exercise of its original jurisdiction

escalation.trigger: An heir or beneficiary thinks the estate needs a bond with surety after surety was waived
escalation.next: Motion to the Staunton Circuit Court to require the personal representative to furnish security (a hearing is held)
escalation.quote: upon the motion of a legatee, devisee, or distributee of an estate, or any person who has a pecuniary interest in an estate, the court or clerk may require the personal representative to furnish security.

escalation.trigger: No affidavit of notice is recorded within four months after qualification
escalation.next: Commissioner of Accounts, who summons the fiduciary and enforces the filing
escalation.quote: If this subsection has not been complied with within four months after qualification, the commissioner of accounts shall issue, through the sheriff or other proper officer, a summons to such fiduciary requiring him to comply

escalation.trigger: The executor or administrator does not file the inventory within four months
escalation.next: Commissioner of Accounts summons the fiduciary; if it is still not filed 30 days after service, the commissioner reports to the Staunton Circuit Court, which can fine the fiduciary up to $500
escalation.quote: the commissioner of accounts shall issue, through the sheriff or other proper officer, a summons to the fiduciary requiring him to make such return.

escalation.trigger: An heir or beneficiary disagrees with the executor's or administrator's inventory or account
escalation.next: Object before the Commissioner of Accounts
escalation.quote: Any interested person, or the next friend of an interested person, may, before the commissioner of accounts, insist upon or object to anything

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the Commissioner of Accounts' report on an account
escalation.next: File exceptions; the Staunton Circuit Court examines them and corrects errors
escalation.deadline: Within 15 days after the report is filed in the Clerk's Office; if no exceptions are filed, the report stands confirmed the next day
escalation.quote: If no exceptions have been filed, the report shall stand confirmed on the day next following the expiration of the period of 15 days after the day on which the report was filed in the clerk's office.

escalation.trigger: A Commissioner of Accounts takes, or fails to take, an action in violation of the statutory duties or the circuit court's requirements (complaints may be made by a person with an interest in a matter before the commissioner)
escalation.next: Written complaint to the Standing Committee on Commissioners of Accounts of the Judicial Council of Virginia, sent to the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia
escalation.basis: Rules for Addressing Complaints Against Commissioners of Accounts (Judicial Council of Virginia, effective April 1, 2021), https://www.vacourts.gov/static/courts/circuit/resources/coa/coa_complaints.pdf
escalation.quote: All Complaints shall be submitted in writing to the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia

escalation.trigger: Probate tax was overpaid (the inventory shows a lower value than the probate tax return)
escalation.next: Refund application to the Virginia Department of Taxation for the state share and, for the city share, to the Staunton City Treasurer
escalation.quote: In the event of an overpayment of such tax, the personal representative may apply to the Department of Taxation and, if a local probate tax was paid, to the treasurer of the city or county for a refund.

escalation.trigger: The Staunton Circuit Court enters a final order you believe is wrong
escalation.next: Court of Appeals of Virginia (notice of appeal)
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days from the date of the final order
escalation.quote: a notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals in any case within the jurisdiction of the court shall be filed within 30 days from the date of any final judgment order

escalation.trigger: You need a disability accommodation at the Clerk's Office, or one is refused
escalation.next: The Clerk of the Staunton Circuit Court; other complaints go through the Office of the Executive Secretary's ADA grievance procedure
escalation.basis: Circuit Courts Informational Pamphlet (ADA notice, revised 7/2026), https://www.vacourts.gov/courts/circuit/circuitinfo.pdf
escalation.quote: Complaints concerning a program, service, or activity of a circuit court clerk's office should be directed to that clerk.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The probate page's copy of 2026-05-11 matches its 2025-11-15 copy except for one link. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

The City's Probate Information Form (f1) is a scanned image with no text layer (PDF created 2023-04-13). Its two quotes (steps 5 and 8) and the description of its questions are transcriptions from the page images, which a text search cannot confirm. It is not fillable. Its wording on nonresidents ('If the person seeking appointment is NOT a Virginia resident agent, you will need a Virginia Resident to either co-qualify ... or to be appointed as the resident') is garbled; step 8 reads it together with CC-1610, which appoints a Virginia resident to receive service of process. State law (§ 64.2-1426) also lets a nonresident qualify with a consent to service on the clerk and a bond with surety, so ask the Clerk whether Staunton insists on a resident co-fiduciary or agent in every case.

Small Estate Affidavit link: the 2026-05-11 copy of the probate page links a City-hosted 'Virginia Small Estate Act Affidavit' as document 13200, which has no Internet Archive copy, so its content is not confirmed. The form is listed here at its statewide source (CC-1685, revised 07/26, $75,000 limit), which matches current § 64.2-601.

Local law: Staunton City Code § 3.70.010 (Chapter 3.70, Probate Tax) is on eCode360 (General Code), whose Terms of Use limit the content to its licensed use, so no Code text is quoted. In lexflow's paraphrase, the section imposes a city probate tax equal to one-third of the state tax under § 58.1-1712, and directs the Clerk of the Circuit Court to collect it, pay it into the city treasury and keep five percent as compensation under §§ 58.1-3805 and 58.1-3806; its history note cites the 1985 Code § 12-270 and an ordinance numbered 12-12-02. eCode360 warns its copy may not reflect the latest legislation.

The wording of § 3.70.010 imposes the city tax on the grant of administration and does not repeat the enabling statute's words about the probate of a will. Step 10 and the fee list therefore say the city share is charged on grants of administration and ask the reader to confirm with the Clerk whether it is also charged when a will is probated with an executor (the clerks' pamphlet gives the local tax as payable 'if applicable').

No City of Staunton $25 local fee for recording a list of heirs or real estate affidavit (the option in §§ 58.1-1717.1 and 58.1-1718(ii)) was found: Chapter 3.70 lists only § 3.70.010. Only the $25 state fee is given.

Clerk fees: the Staunton Clerk publishes no itemized probate fee list on the pages cited here. The fees given are the statutory amounts. How the Clerk applies recording fees to wills and lists of heirs, whether it charges the $3 bond fee in § 17.1-275(A)(6), and which payment methods it accepts for probate (cash, check, card) were not confirmed. The Clerk's page mentions a convenience fee only for online payment of court fines and costs.

The City's probate page says the Clerk 'collects the applicable estate taxes for the Commonwealth'. What the Clerk collects at probate is the probate tax (state and city), not Virginia estate tax; the statewide CC-1651 instructions say the probate tax is not an inheritance or estate tax.

Appointments: the City's probate page does not say probate is by appointment only, and no Staunton probate phone extension or scheduling page was found. The City's form refers to 'the appointment', and the statewide CC-1650 instructions say to call for one.

Venue: that some homes outside the city limits in Augusta County have Staunton mailing addresses is general knowledge, not from a source cited here. The Augusta Circuit Court address (100 Dick Huff Lane, Verona) and the Waynesboro Circuit Court address (250 South Wayne Avenue, Waynesboro) are from their vacourts.gov pages, both of which list the 25th Judicial Circuit.

Electronic devices: the Staunton Circuit Court's Policy Regarding Portable Electronic Devices on vacourts.gov is a scanned image signed 6/10/2026 with no text layer, so it is described, not quoted. It replaces earlier policies; the City's visitor page (capture of 2025-11-15) links a City-hosted policy document whose URL version stamp suggests mid-2020 (an inference from the URL), and says devices are not permitted in the building. Under the 2026 policy visitors may keep a device only if the Sheriff determines they pose no security risk and need it for their business; check at the security entrance.

Privacy: the City and vacourts.gov pages name the elected Clerk, the judges, the ADA Coordinator and other staff, and the Treasurer's page links a personal staff mailbox. None of these names or personal addresses are recorded. The Commissioner of Accounts directory (updated as of 8/31/2026) lists commissioners for Staunton; they are individual attorneys, so no names or contact details are recorded. Use the directory or ask the Clerk.

Commissioner of Accounts fees: the Staunton Circuit Court's own fee schedule was not found. The amounts given are the statewide Uniform Fee Schedule Guidelines, which the vacourts.gov page says to confirm with the local circuit court.

The 'Probate in Virginia' pamphlet (Virginia Court Clerks' Association, republished July 2019) linked from the City's page gives a $50,000 limit for small-asset estates. Current Va. Code § 64.2-601(A)(1) and the CC-1685 form (revised 07/26) say $75,000. The pamphlet's probate tax figures ($1.00 state and .33 local per $1,000) match 10 cents per $100 plus one-third.

The CC-1651 Probate Tax Return's preparation note says the form 'must be completed if the value of the estate exceeds $10,000', but the form itself and Va. Code § 58.1-1714 say $15,000. The statute governs.

Some statewide instructions are old: CC-1650 instructions are dated 07/03 and 07/13 and quote an earlier wording of the nursing-home presumption, and CC-1608 instructions cite repealed §§ 64.1-1 and 64.1-11 (now in Title 64.2). The City's form, rather than CC-1650, is what the Staunton page links; whether the Clerk also wants CC-1650 was not confirmed.
'A Guide to the Administration of Decedents' Estates in Virginia', linked from the City's page through the Virginia Bar Association's site, is not an official government source and is not used here.

Free legal help: the City's probate page links the Virginia State Bar's Free and Low-Cost Legal Resources pamphlet and Virginia Free Legal Answers. They were not read, and no statement that the Clerk's Office cannot give legal advice was found on a Staunton page.

Not covered in detail: administrators appointed only for wrongful death or personal injury suits (§ 64.2-454), curators beyond the escalation note (§ 64.2-451), guardianships of minors and incapacitated adults (also handled by the Clerk, per the City's page), corporate fiduciaries, estate debts and creditor claims, and federal or state income and estate tax returns.

Appeal scope: § 64.2-445 lets 'any person interested in the probate of the will' appeal an order the Clerk entered under § 64.2-444, which includes appointment orders. Whether that six-month appeal also reaches a Clerk's appointment of an administrator when there is no will was not confirmed.

Not confirmed by lexflow's software: the words once quoted for the step 'Fill in the City of Staunton Probate Information Form and gather what to bring' and the step 'If an executor or administrator lives outside Virginia, arrange a Virginia resident' (https://www.ci.staunton.va.us/home/showpublisheddocument/12029/638423099097970000) were not found on the cited page as lexflow read it (the cited page could not be read (robots.txt for www.ci.staunton.va.us answered HTTP 403, so robots.txt disallows https://www.ci.staunton.va.us/home/showpublisheddocument/12029/638423099097970000; the PDF has no text layer lexflow can read); the form is a scan with no text layer, so a text search cannot read it (lexflow read the Internet Archive copy, the City's site refusing automated readers)). Those claims now rest on the cited page as read, without a matched quote; check them at the link before relying on them.

s6: the draft said a witness could give a deposition 'before a notary on the state forms (CC-1601 to CC-1604)'. The forms show the CC-1601 to CC-1603 depositions are sworn before a clerk, deputy clerk or notary public, and CC-1604 is not a deposition: two disinterested people swear to it before the Clerk or a deputy clerk, and it also serves for a will of a person in military service. Rewritten from the forms, with §§ 64.2-403(B) and 64.2-447(A) (including the withdrawal of the will for a deposition).

s7: the draft said 'Anyone appointed ... swears they are not under a legal disability or convicted of certain felonies'. § 64.2-502(D) sets that oath for administrators of estates without a will, so the step now says so, lists the felonies and gives the sole-heir exception; the disability bar for administration with the will annexed is from § 64.2-500(B). Also: added designees, the 45-day nonprofit conservator or guardian rule (§ 64.2-502(A)(3)), the executor's failure to give bond, death, resignation or removal, and the desertion or abandonment bar (§§ 64.2-500(C), 64.2-502(E)); the 30-day fallback now uses the statute's 'person who would have been entitled to administration' rather than 'a person who would inherit'.

s8: added what state law allows without a Virginia co-fiduciary (consent to service on the Clerk or a named resident, § 64.2-1426(A)), that a nonresident needs surety even if the will waives it, that the $35,000 surety waiver is at the Clerk's discretion (§ 64.2-1411(A)), and the clerks' pamphlet's co-fiduciary note. The City's practice and the state rule are now told apart, with a prompt to ask the Clerk.

s10: the draft stated the city tax applies to every probate. Staunton City Code § 3.70.010, re-read on eCode360 (not quoted), imposes it on the grant of administration only, so the step and the fee entry now say that and tell the reader to confirm with the Clerk for probate with an executor. Also added the $25 minimum for additional tax or refunds, the probate-estate exclusions from CC-1651, and the 'reasonable estimate' rule from the CC-1651 instructions.
